name: Zoho Books
tagline: Invoicing, banking, expenses, inventory, projects, and tax workflows

pricing.freeTierCaps: Annual revenue below $50,000; 1 user + 1 accountant; 1,000 invoices/year; 1,000 expenses/year; 50 scans/month; 5 scheduled reports
pricing.hiddenCosts: Each subscription covers 1 organization; additional organizations require separate subscriptions. Extra users and some payment, tax, and ecosystem integrations cost extra.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Zoho Books's durable value is banking, compliance, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private small-business accounting ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: CSV exports from the user's own accounts
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations
live bank feeds and payment rails
whyPeopleStillPay: Zoho Books: People pay because errors touch real money. Bank connections, reconciliation, tax changes, evidence, security, and support are the product.
ongoingBurden: Own data integrity, backups, import mapping, reconciliation, security, audit logs, tax changes, and recovery.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Local-first open-source personal finance and envelope budgeting.

priorArt.name: Invoice Ninja
priorArt.desc: Open-source invoicing, payments, and client management.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Invoices, banking, expenses, inventory, projects and tax rules in one ERP; setup is the first project.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext can model the work but takes substantially more setup and does not match Zoho Books' turnkey bank connections, country tax automation, e-invoicing links, mobile apps, and hosted integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Billing, banks, expenses, stock and projects in one practical suite; local tax filing remains external.

facts.install: DoliWamp, DoliDeb, DoliRPM, Docker, or a conventional PHP web-server installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records live in MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, while uploaded and generated documents live in Dolibarr's documents directory or mounted volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dolibarr's local tax, e-invoicing, bank-feed, and payment integrations are much less turnkey than Zoho Books and often require modules or manual configuration.
facts.setupBlocker: A packaged desktop-style installer exists on some platforms, but a durable deployment still needs a web server or Docker, database, HTTPS, backups, updates, and localization.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: Invoices, reconciliation, expenses, inventory and project tracking on one desktop; collaboration is manual.

facts.install: Native desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.dataFormat: Each business is stored in a local .manager file backed by SQLite, including its accounting records and attached documents; the user chooses and backs up that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Manager Desktop is local and collaboration-light, without Zoho Books' managed bank feeds, tax and e-invoicing automation, client access, mobile workflow, and connected app suite.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Accounting, invoices, stock, projects and reports; polished tax automation is not part of the bargain.

facts.install: Docker Compose is the shortest documented path; packages and manual Perl installation also exist
facts.dataFormat: Companies and accounting records live in PostgreSQL databases; uploaded or generated documents live in the configured document store or server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: LedgerSMB offers a serious ledger but not Zoho Books' polished country-specific tax automation, bank feeds, mobile experience, client collaboration, and integration catalog.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real web stack, Docker, PostgreSQL, administrator credentials, a reverse proxy and TLS for internet use, plus backups and upgrades.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Credibility row: Zoho Books survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Zoho Books; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private small-business accounting ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations; live bank feeds and payment rails; tax and accounting rule updates.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
